title: Where Hungary Is - Hol van Magyarország?

sections.title: Welcome to Citizenship
body: This is a 36-unit track about Hungary itself: where it is and what it stands for; a thousand years of history, from the Carpathian Basin before the Magyars to the regime change of 1989–90; and how the country works today, from the *Alaptörvény* to its institutions, symbols and holidays. It covers the ground of the *alkotmányos alapismeretek* exam, the test on basic constitutional knowledge that most applicants for Hungarian citizenship have to pass in Hungarian.

Every lesson is built around a story: a real episode told as a narrative, not a list of facts to memorise. The words you need come from that story, and so does one B1 grammar point, practised on the same topic. Each unit has five lessons, then a consolidation lesson that ties them together.

This track runs alongside Core Hungarian, not instead of it. It doesn't gate your level test, but it assumes you're working through B1 Core grammar at the same time, and every word you learn here goes into the same review deck.

To be clear about one thing: this track teaches the exam's topics in Hungarian at B1. It isn't an official preparation course, so check the current requirements and materials with the authorities before you sit it.
Okay, let's start with the map.

sections.title: Lesson Goals
items: I can explain where Hungary is located, using Közép-Európában and a Kárpát-medencében.
I can state Hungary's approximate size and population.
I can explain why Hungarian belongs to the Finno-Ugric language family, unlike most of its neighbours' languages.
I can describe how Budapest relates to the country's counties.
I can use van/vannak correctly when describing where something is located.
